title: RasaLanka Machine-Generated Annotation Format Specification
purpose: Defines one JSON record per image as a machine-generated candidate for later human adjudication. The format preserves provenance, uncertainty and out-of-scope observations without asserting verified labels.

dependencies.jsonschema: >=4.18 (validated with 4.26.0 and its transitive packages attrs 26.1.0, jsonschema-specifications 2025.9.1, referencing 0.37.0, rpds-py 2026.9.1)
dependencies.note: jsonschema was installed into the local Python environment with 'python -m pip install jsonschema'. It is the only new direct dependency; it is used by scripts/validate_annotation_schema.py. No application runtime dependency and no requirements/pyproject file were introduced.

differences: Machine records are candidates, not adjudicated ground truth.
Machine records have no annotator_id or annotation_timestamp; those are human-only concepts.
Machine labels are objects carrying class_id, confidence and status; human labels are plain class ID arrays.
Machine records store source provenance (folder, filename, SHA-256, relative path) for every image.
Human verification defaults to false and cannot be asserted without evidence.
The two schema files and their $id values are separate; neither overwrites the other.

annotation_id.meaning: Globally unique ID for this annotation record. 128-bit random hex after the MA- prefix.

image_id.meaning: Globally unique, stable image ID. Independent of folder, filename and hash so re-annotation keeps identity.

batch_id.meaning: Processing batch that produced the record, for traceability and rollback.

original_folder.meaning: Ingredient folder name copied verbatim. Never renamed or normalised in place.

original_filename.type: non-empty string with no path separators
original_filename.meaning: Original filename only. Preserves the source identifier.

relative_path.meaning: Path relative to collected_dataset root; enables re-reading the exact source image.

image_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of original image bytes. Content identity for deduplication, not proof of licence or ownership.

folder_proposed_class.type: approved in-scope class ID or null
folder_proposed_class.meaning: Single candidate from folder_class_mapping.json. Null whenever the folder is ambiguous, out of scope or unmapped.

folder_mapping_status.meaning: Confidence class of the folder proposal. No value makes a folder name ground truth.

machine_labels.meaning: In-scope ingredient labels with class_id, confidence and status. Multiple labels are permitted.

uncertain_labels.meaning: Candidate in-scope classes that could not be resolved. Preserved for human review rather than dropped.

out_of_scope_labels.meaning: Visible but non-target classes from the approved out-of-scope list, retained as observations/hard negatives.

visible_ingredient_count.meaning: Count of visibly distinct ingredient items; can be greater than the number of resolved labels.

multi_ingredient_scene.meaning: True when more than one distinct ingredient is visible. Must be true if machine_labels has more than one entry.

quality_flags.meaning: Automated screening results only. Every flag is heuristic and needs human confirmation before acting on it.

processing_state_evidence.meaning: Visible processing attributes such as dried, powder or paste. These are attributes, not new ingredient classes.

processing_status.meaning: Where the candidate is in the machine pipeline.

human_review.meaning: Human verification metadata. Absent evidence means not verified.

annotation_method.meaning: Fixed discriminator that prevents confusion with human annotation records.

generator.meaning: How the labels were produced: folder_proposal, automated_heuristic, model_prediction or hybrid, plus real model identifiers.

processing_notes.meaning: Free text explaining decisions, warnings and unresolved ambiguity.

label_object.description: All three label arrays use objects with the same three required keys.

class_id.meaning: In-scope ID for machine_labels and uncertain_labels; out-of-scope ID for out_of_scope_labels.

confidence.meaning: Real model confidence only. Null is mandatory when no model prediction exists; never fabricate a value.

status.meaning: predicted | folder_proposed | needs_review for machine_labels; uncertain for uncertain_labels; out_of_scope for out_of_scope_labels.

human_verified.meaning: True only after a real human review, with verifier ID and timestamp recorded.

verified_by.meaning: Real verifier identity. Never fabricated or inferred.

verification_timestamp.meaning: Real review time. Never fabricated or inferred.

validation_rules: The JSON Schema itself must be a valid Draft 2020-12 schema.
Every permitted class ID in the schema must exactly match approved_taxonomy.json; no IDs are invented.
human_verified = true requires verified_by, verification_timestamp and review_status = reviewed.
confidence is either a number in [0,1] or null; null is valid and is the default.
If generator.method is folder_proposal, every machine_labels confidence must be null.
If generator.model_id is null, every machine_labels confidence must be null.
machine_labels and uncertain_labels may only use in-scope class IDs.
out_of_scope_labels may only use approved out-of-scope IDs.
multi_ingredient_scene = false implies at most one machine label.
No folder name is accepted as ground truth; all non-approved mappings require human review.

folder_mapping.rule: Mappings are proposals. proposed_class_id is null for ambiguous, out-of-scope and unmapped folders. Never force an uncertain mapping into a class.

example_valid_record.processing_notes: Folder-based proposal only; no model prediction has been run.

prohibited_practices: Copying a folder name directly into a verified/human label.
Assigning confidence without an actual model output.
Creating a new class ID or silently merging two classes.
Filling in annotator IDs or review timestamps before a human review.
Generating annotations for the full image set before this format is approved.
